existing_issues.issue: Level 5 looks too high. Italian conservatory syllabi use Polo's 30 double-stop studies far earlier: Vibo Valentia CB54 sets 'the first ones' for the year-1 exam and the set for the final exam of the basic course (positions up to the 5th), next to Kayser Op. 20, Mazas Op. 36, Dont Op. 37, Sitt Op. 32; Cuneo (2017) places it in pre-academic period B1-B2 with Kayser and Sitt; the row's own exam list (RCM 6-8) also points to L2-L4. Title is right (IMSLP: 30 Studi a corde doppie).

Note says 'also used by violists', but the caprices were written for the viola: IMSLP gives instrumentation 'viola (or violin) (read frontispiece)' and Italian Wikipedia lists '41 Capricci per l'alto-viola'. Title, opus and level are fine; suggested note: 'Written for viola (or violin); Classical-era caprices on bowing, shifting and double stops'.

IMPORTANT for the other researchers: scripts/expand/imslp_author.py only reads the main author category, so collections and methods filed under '<Author>/Collections' or '<Author>/Books' are missed (Campagnoli returned 2 pages, but Op. 10, 12, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22 are in /Collections and /Books; Rolla's scales, intonazioni and duo-studies are not in the main category either). Fix: also read 'Category:<Author>/Collections', '/Collected Works', '/Books', or use the API list=search with the quoted name, e.g. srsearch="Campagnoli, Bartolomeo"; note the response uses 'query-continue' (not 'continue') for paging. intitle: search returns nothing on IMSLP.
